title: Complete Houses, Tom Kundig
body_html:
The definitive collection of residential work by celebrated contemporary architect Tom Kundig

Tom Kundig is one of the most sought-after architects working today, known for his extraordinary houses that deeply engage with their surrounding environment. 

Based in the Pacific Northwest, Kundig’s international portfolio includes homes built into rocky sites, dynamic kinetic devices that open walls and roofs, and even moving architecture that travels via railroad track. 

Spanning nearly four decades of design, Tom Kundig: Complete Houses presents 462 residential projects together for the first time.

title: Panafold Issue 4
body_html:
The Panafold is a print-only quarterly magazine celebrating California arts, architecture, design, and culture.

In this issue: PETER SHIRE crafts a technicolor universe where humor, joy, and play reign; MARIAH NIELSON stewards JB BLUNK’s legacy while shaping her own; RAFI AJL’s sculptural designs gesture towards the ineffable; color, material, and sensory perception converge in YUNHEE MIN’s luminous abstractions; with WAKA WAKA, SHIN OKUDA transforms humble materials into revelatory form; at the NORTON SIMON MUSEUM, MIMI ZEIGER traces EDITH HEATH’s enduring influence on modern architecture; RAIMONDS STAPRANS coaxes light out of pigment; new poems by ROBERT HASS and CHRISTINE LARUSSO; essays, criticism, & more…

title: Untapped Print Edition 003
body_html:
Untapped is a design journal that looks back to look forward.

Our stories identify important knowledge about improving the built environment, and contextualize it for today and tomorrow.

Edition 003 Features stories by Jonathan Nesci, Jesse Dorris, Jeremy Bilotti and David Rosenwasser, Edwin Heathcote, Michele Oka Doner, Diana Budds, Charlie Schuck, Kate Wagner, Sarah Archer, and Peter Miller.

title: Para Llevar, ISSUE 6: MARMOTA
body_html: In our first bilingual issue we find ourselves south of the border in the vast metropolis of Mexico City at the casual homestyled Roma haunt, Marmota. The staff is like family, painting and writing and riding motorcycles on the side. The open kitchen  serves up fare influenced by the Pacific Northwest, where the husband and wife duo, Federico and Poppy, both spent time working in the same kitchen, albeit at different times.

title: Para Llevar, ISSUE 5: FLOUR+WATER // PENNY ROMA
body_html: In our first flip cover issue we hang out at the Mission District icon Flour + Water, and its sister restaurant down the 20th St. corridor, Penny Roma. They offer an annual artist grant to one employee each year to complete a creative project, as well as multiple education grants to further staff development in everything from language and wine to floral design. It shows in the service.
